top_story: Washington’s move on 28 August to sanction Banque Misr’s UAE branches for channeling more than $1 billion through Iranian shadow banking networks sharpened pressure on Tehran just as Iran deepened domestic repression by moving to criminalise any contact with foreign media. That pairing reflects a converging external and internal containment dynamic: financial restrictions tighten Iran’s regional economic room, while the proposed media ban seeks to sever citizens, journalists, and dissidents from outside scrutiny. In Gaza, Israeli strikes on 29 August killed four people and damaged a hospital supply warehouse, extending a baseline pattern in which military operations steadily erode civilian survival systems as casualties rise and people remain trapped under rubble. The regional picture is one of coercive control exercised through both finance and force, with civilians bearing the immediate cost and civic space contracting further.
